Right you are and the untested alternate approach had erroneous code: df1[1:3][ !duplicated(df1[1:3] ]. These are the unique categories that you could "apply" ( or split?) over. I'm thinking it might have been more "strategic" to rbind/stack these dataframes and add membership indicator.

> My dataset has multiple years of data and I want to subset just how I did it with 'a' and 'b' and apply a t.test. Also, instead of returning a list, could the t.test statistic be stored in a dataframe.

Actually `mapply` returns a matrix, but because the results of `t.test` are a list, it was a matrix of lists. (If you used sapply you might oversimplify the results.) If you want just one or two parts of the result of t.test, then you need to say which parts:

Value

A list with class "htest" containing the following components:

statistic
the value of the t-statistic.

parameter
the degrees of freedom for the t-statistic.

p.value
the p-value for the test.

conf.int
a confidence interval for the mean appropriate to the specified alternative hypothesis.

estimate
the estimated mean or difference in means depending on whether it was a one-sample test or a two-sample test.

null.value
the specified hypothesized value of the mean or mean difference depending on whether it was a one-sample test or a two-sample test.

alternative
a character string describing the alternative hypothesis.

method
a character string indicating what type of t-test was performed.

data.name
a character string giving the name(s) of the data.

messages.subject: Re: t.test of matching columns from two datasets using plyr
parts:
On Aug 15, 2014, at 9:35 AM, Felipe Carrillo wrote:

> David, I want to extract the t-statistic of the test and make a dataframe of each var1-sp1. Even if I have to do a t.test with one variable from each dataset at a time would be fine.
> Based on the results of:

> a <- subset(df1,Year=='1995' & month=='Apr' & newRegion=='West')
> > b <- subset(df2,Year=='1995' & month=='Apr' & newRegion=='West')
>

> since both 'a' and 'b' have un-equal number of records, wouldn't be appropriate to do a loop instead to be able to capture all the records from both datasets and do a t.test of var1-sp1, var2-sp2 and so on...?
> I know that loops could be slow and some users are against it but I wouldn't mind using it here. My problem is that I successfully can loop through one variable (either month, newRegion or Year) but I fail with a nested loop trying to use all the variables at the same time.
>

You define an interaction variable and could single-loop over unique values of interaction(Year, Month, Region):


> This is the loop that I was attempting without success:
>
> species.emp <- c('var1','var2','var3','sp1','sp2','sp3') # I might need to change sp1,sp2,sp3 to #var1,var2 and var3 respectively

Might want to create a list of paired variable name vectors

> year.set <- c(1995:1998)
> month.set <- c('Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug')
> region.set <- c('North','South','West','Far West')
>
out <- matrix(NA, nrow=length(unique(species.emp),
ncol=3, dimnames=list(rows=unique(species.emp),
cols=c('var1','var2','var3') )


> for(species in species.emp){
> for(year in year.set){
> for(month in month.set){
> for(region in region.set){
>
> ok.df1 <- df1$Year==year &
> df1$month==month &
> df1$newRegion==region
> y.df1 <- df1$species[ok.df1]
>
> ok.df2 <- df2$Year==year &
> df2$Month==month &
> df2$newRegion==region
> y.df2 <- df2$species[ok.emp]
>
> out <- t.test(x=y.df1,y=y.df2, var.equal=TRUE) # apply a t.test to each combination

If you want to avoid another loop you could make three similar copies of the t.test-call. Still not sure what your desired output should be, but could just be:


out['species', 1:3] <- c( t.test(x=y.df1$var1,y=y.df2$sp1, var.equal=TRUE)$statistic,
t.test(x=y.df1$var2,y=y.df2$sp2, var.equal=TRUE)$statistic
t.test(x=y.df1var3,y=y.df2$sp3, var.equal=TRUE)$statistic)

> }}}
>

> Actually `mapply` returns a matrix, but because the results of `t.test` are a list, it was a matrix of lists. (If you used sapply you might oversimplify the results.) If you want just one or two parts of the result of t.test, then you need to say which parts:
>
> Value
>
> A list with class "htest" containing the following components:
>
> statistic
> the value of the t-statistic.
>
> parameter
> the degrees of freedom for the t-statistic.
>
> p.value
> the p-value for the test.
>
> conf.int
> a confidence interval for the mean appropriate to the specified alternative hypothesis.
>
> estimate
> the estimated mean or difference in means depending on whether it was a one-sample test or a two-sample test.
>
> null.value
> the specified hypothesized value of the mean or mean difference depending on whether it was a one-sample test or a two-sample test.
>
> alternative
> a character string describing the alternative hypothesis.
>
> method
> a character string indicating what type of t-test was performed.
>
> data.name
> a character string giving the name(s) of the data.
>
